Scientific Claim Statement: Identification and causal behavioral intervention of targeted latent circuits for embodied spatial navigation.
Validation Status: FALSIFIED AS MODULAR CIRCUIT; UNRESOLVED REPRESENTATION HYPOTHESIS
Primary Empirical Proof: C1 ablation drop (3.3%) is non-selective compared to random 8D subspace drops (20.8% +/- 14.8%, p=0.9032, z=-1.177). Random 8D subspace patching achieves higher offline donor cosine (0.9854 vs 0.9779) and equivalent rescue (90.9% vs 93.3%, p=0.6129), falsifying modular isolation and precluding selective rescue. Circuit C1 remains an unresolved representation hypothesis.
Hardware Silicon Verification: Hardware RTL self-checking testbench validates bit-exact concordance with software fixed-point core.

Scientific Claim Statement: Hierarchical macro temporal abstraction amortizes latency and bounds multi-step open-loop kinematic drift.
Validation Status: VALIDATED (Latency Amortization & Open-Loop Stability; Closed-Loop Parity with Micro & Kinematic Heuristic)
Primary Empirical Proof: Open-loop macro direct prediction cuts 5-step displacement error from 0.081m to 0.046m (-43.5%). In closed loop (N=50), macro (46.0%) achieves parity with recursive micro (50.0%, p=0.7266) and straight-line kinematic heuristic (46.0%, p=1.0000) with 4.30x measured GPU latency reduction (0.371 ms vs 1.594 ms). Under Holm-Bonferroni correction over 6 comparisons, macro vs shuffled binding (unadjusted p=0.03125) has adjusted p=0.1562 > 0.05.
Hardware Silicon Verification: Direct KR260 FPGA silicon execution: 4,327 cycles (34.61 us) at 125 MHz, 3,579 LUTs (3.06%), 0.365 W, zero DDR4 access.

Scientific Claim Statement: Embodied visual navigation dynamically grounds target objects when visible in camera frustum while task conditioning is constrained by visual saliency.
Validation Status: VALIDATED & DISENTANGLED (Dynamic Visual Grounding Confirmed Under Visibility; Token Semantic Map Alone Falsified)
Primary Empirical Proof: In Phase 3 benchmark v2 (N=30 per condition, initial dist >= 0.60m, relocation >= 0.75m, post-action evaluation), visible relocated target achieves 73.3% success (22/30, median path 0.488m) requiring active locomotion, showing significant degradation from canonical 100.0% (McNemar p=0.03125). In paired scenes where candidate objects A and B are simultaneously visible in identical RGB frame, changing task token rotates goal vector by 0.869 rad (49.8 deg) with 66.7%/70.0% success and 20.0% dual discrimination rate, demonstrating token conditioning interacts causally with visual saliency.
Hardware Silicon Verification: Deterministic embedded execution with verified timing closure and zero memory leakage.

Scientific Claim Statement: Learned collision predictions provide a prospective safety constraint for dynamic obstacle avoidance.
Validation Status: FALSIFIED AS PROSPECTIVE BARRIER (High Offline Discrimination AUROC=1.0 Does Not Translate to Closed-Loop Safety)
Primary Empirical Proof: Offline K=5 macro prospective metrics show AUROC=1.0000 with clustered bootstrap 95% CI = [0.5, 1.0] across 20 episode clusters, Brier=0.0003, ECE=0.0041, FNR=0.0%. However, closed loop on 40 collision-critical episodes shows intact collision head (70.0% collisions) is identical to shuffled binding (70.0%, p=1.0000) and disabled collision head (70.0%, p=1.0000), while random predictor yields 57.5% (p=0.0625) and oracle physics simulation reduces collisions to 7.5% (p=5.96e-8). Refutes formal Control Barrier Function (CBF) claims.
Hardware Silicon Verification: FPGA pipeline latency bounds reaction time but safety requires geometric margin rather than contact-level neural prediction.

Scientific Claim Statement: Egocentric goal memory operates as an external controller heuristic rather than an essential learned recurrent world model state.
Validation Status: VALIDATED (Controller Heuristic Decoupled; Occlusion Tracking Benefit Identified)
Primary Empirical Proof: Goal memory is handwritten Python logic in model_wrappers.py (0.65 visual + 0.35 memory) utilizing learned 2D micro_ego_head displacements. Under continuous vision, visual-only matches blended control (96.7% vs 96.7%). Under 10-step visual sensory blackout (steps 5..15), visual-only control suffers +0.097m higher tracking error (p=3.79e-6) than blended memory, proving memory causally maintains egocentric tracking during visual deprivation, while final navigation success recovers to 83.3% upon restoration (non-inferior within delta=0.10 margin to full memory 80.0%).
Hardware Silicon Verification: Zero state retention required on FPGA accelerator; pure visual pipeline operates stateless per step.
